evidence_excerpts: When faced with a case in which it seems that [p] is fully grounded in D yet ~ 0(∧D → p), the advocate of necessity should check to see if there are additional explanatorily relevant facts P such that 0(∧(D, P) → p).
Hence, it seems that the proponent of this putative counterexample, rather than mistaking a mere partial ground for a complete ground, mistakes a non-ground for a ground.
text: Putative counterexamples to the necessity of grounding typically misidentify a merely partial ground, or even a non-ground, as a full ground.
